requirement:
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.targets`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.

An anchored file or node MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
{cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`, by an input selecting it, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.

Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such
as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the
definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
rationale:
The anchors requirement is implemented and marked, and tests cover its main cases and failure cases. I did not run the tests; this is from reading the code and test sources.

**Declaration syntax and option errors**
- `definition_blocks` (src/lib.rs) reads `:name: value` lines directly after the opening fence, using `option_line`. It stops at the first non-option line and does not parse options for `{definition}` blocks.
- `collect_definitions` (src/evidence.rs) maps `:impl:` to an `{impl}` edge for `{req}`. It maps `:test:` to a `{test}` edge for `{req}` and `{example}`.
- It reports a validation error for any other option, including `:impl:` on an example. It also reports an empty value with the file, line, kind and definition name.
- `Anchor::parse` splits `path#selector` on the first `#`, so selectors with a `#N` suffix still work.

**Option lines excluded from text and rendering**
- `without_options` strips option lines from the definition text, `raw_lines` and requirements inputs. `preprocess_book` and `replace_definitions` use `text_start`, so options are not rendered as body text.
- `anchor_options_are_metadata_not_body_text` (src/lib.rs) shows that only lines immediately after the fence are options. A later `:test:` line and an inline `:impl:` stay in the body.
- `requirements_inputs_omit_option_lines` checks the stripped text, line ranges and `raw_lines`. `every_definition_gets_a_nested_detail_page_without_an_index` checks the detail pages.

**Resolution and evidence coverage**
- `Anchor::resolve` uses `OutlineCache::parse`, which goes through `read_project_file`, `check_project_file` and `resolve_evidence_file`. These apply the containment and permission rules from `ci.schema`. The selector is resolved with `ParsedSource::resolve`.
- `validate_references` requires an evidence input that selects the anchored node or one of its ancestors. Otherwise it reports "no input selects … anchored by :impl:".
- An anchor that does not resolve is reported with the evidence file, the anchor label, the definition name and its source location.
- `anchored_files_must_be_completely_covered_and_resolvable` and `selector_anchors_are_covered_by_inputs_selecting_the_node_or_an_ancestor` (src/evidence.rs) cover these cases. They include a root-node anchor that a section input does not cover, an ancestor input that does cover it, a missing file, a missing selector, and stale evidence after the anchored file changes.
- `unsupported_and_empty_options_are_validation_errors` covers the unsupported-option and empty-value errors.

**Authoring before inference**
- `AssessmentSources::prepare` (src/authoring/inputs.rs) checks permission and resolution for each anchor before any inference. Failures are reported as `<subject>: cannot read :impl: anchor <label>: …`. Resolved anchors become mandatory outline inputs.
- `anchored_files_contribute_root_node_inputs` and `unreadable_or_denied_anchors_fail_before_inference` test the inputs. The second test covers both a missing file and a path denied by `habeas.toml` (a `PermissionDenied` error).
- `references_contribute_their_owning_outline_nodes` covers a selector anchor.

**Anchors as edges**
- The `references` tool reports anchors as `impl` or `test` sites with `line: null` and the selector as `item`. It omits excluded files. `references_report_anchors_as_file_or_node_sites` tests this, including a disallowed file.
- `DefinitionEdges::current` (src/index.rs) groups inputs by anchor edges. `detail_inputs_are_grouped_by_current_edges_in_disclosures` tests this.
- The reference-set digest includes anchors. That behaviour belongs to `ci.reference_set`, not to this requirement.

**Skill guidance**
- `assets/skills/habeas-requirements/SKILL.md` is anchored from the requirement declaration, so it appears as an `impl` site with no line. It tells agents to use `:impl:` and `:test:` options only when a file cannot or should not carry a reference. It also says not to anchor a file when a more precise reference exists, such as a comment on the Rust item.

**Marking and open points**
- The relevant functions and structs carry `{impl}` markers. I found no unmarked anchor-specific code.
- One minor point: `prepare` silently skips an anchor to default-excluded generated evidence, while validation would not treat it as unreadable. That skip comes from `authoring.generated_inputs`, and I treat it as outside this requirement.
- No FIXME comments are involved.

text: :::{req} anchors
A `{req}` declaration MAY list `:impl:` and `:test:` options, and an `{example}`
declaration MAY list `:test:` options, immediately after its opening fence and
before its body, one per option line, naming a project file path or
`path#selector` for one outline node under
{cite}`requirements.references.outline_selectors`. Each anchor MUST be an `{impl}` or `{test}` edge, under
{cite}`requirements.references.targets`, from the definition to the anchored file or
node, for files that cannot or should not carry a reference themselves.
Paths MUST follow the path rules in {cite}`requirements.ci.schema`. Option lines
MUST NOT form part of the definition's text for evidence comparison or for
requirements inputs, and MUST NOT render as body text.
An anchored file or node MUST be covered by the definition's evidence under
{cite}`requirements.references.evidence_coverage`, by an input selecting it, so changing the file makes that evidence stale. A path or selector that
does not resolve to a readable, permitted file or node MUST be a validation error naming the
definition and the path; authoring MUST report it before inference, because the
definition cannot be assessed without it. Any other option line in a `{req}` or
`{example}` declaration MUST be a validation error.
Agents SHOULD NOT anchor a file when a more precise reference is available, such
as a reference attached to the Rust item that implements or tests the
definition. Habeas's bundled agent skills MUST give this direction.
:::{req} outline_selectors
An outline selector MUST be a `/`-separated path of segments from the file's
root node to an outline node; the empty selector MUST select the root node. A
named node's segment MUST be `kind[name]`. An anonymous node's segment MUST be
`kind@hash`, where `hash` is the first twelve hexadecimal digits of its identity
hash under {cite}`requirements.references.structural_hash`. Siblings whose
segments would otherwise be identical MUST be disambiguated by `#N`, their
one-based position among those siblings in source order, except `line` nodes:
identical lines are interchangeable, so a `line` selector MUST resolve when any
line with that content exists in the file. In names, `%`, `[`, `]`, `/`, `#`,
`@`, and whitespace MUST be percent-encoded as UTF-8 bytes, so selectors are
reversible. Line numbers MUST NOT form part of a selector.
:::{req} targets

Project text files MAY use the `{impl}`, `{cite}`, and `{test}` roles with a backtick-delimited full requirement or example name. Each reference is a directed edge between its source and the named definition. A source is a project source item or a requirement or example declaration. `{cite}` MUST mean that the source relies on, supports, or refers to the definition, and is an edge from the source to the definition. `{impl}` MUST mean that the source implements part of the definition: it makes a decision, performs a check, produces an output, or handles a case that the definition specifies. A requirement MAY implement part of another requirement by refining one of its obligations. Calling code that implements a definition, or producing a result a caller uses to meet it, MUST NOT by itself count as implementing it. A requirement stating a convention for every output of a kind, such as every validation error, is implemented by the source that carries out the convention as a whole, such as the step that collects and reports those outputs. `{test}` MUST mean that the source is designed to verify behavior the definition specifies: a test through its scenario and the assertions about that scenario's outcome, or a named example through the concrete case it describes. `{impl}` and `{test}` are edges from the definition to the source. Only requirements and examples are assessed; code is reviewed as part of the definitions it implements or tests. Habeas MUST find these references throughout project source files and MUST fail with the source file and line if a name has no matching `{req}` or `{example}` definition. In Markdown, escaped roles and roles in code examples MUST remain literal. Evidence snapshots and generated build output MUST NOT be counted as additional source references: discovery MUST skip `.git` and `target` directories at any depth and the project-root `book` and `evidence` directories.
```text
{impl}`requirements.references.targets`
{cite}`requirements.references.targets`
{test}`requirements.references.targets`
:::{req} schema

A requirement or example evidence file at `evidence/<full-name>.json` MUST be a JSON object with exactly `requirement` or `example`, `determination`, `rationale`, `references`, and `inputs`. `references` MUST be the reference-set digest defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.reference_set`. The definition text and rationale MUST be nonempty strings, `determination` MUST use one of the outcomes defined by {cite}`requirements.ci.outcomes`, and `inputs` MUST be an array. Every evidence input MUST have exactly one of three forms: an outline input with `file`, `item`, and `hash`; a requirements input with `requirements`, `matches`, and `text`; or a definition input with `definition` and `text`. File paths MUST resolve to permitted inputs under {cite}`requirements.ci.input_containment`. Project-local paths SHOULD be recorded relative to the project for portability; absolute and parent-relative paths MAY be used when their resolved targets are permitted. `matches` MUST be an array of distinct full definition names, `hash` MUST be a lowercase hexadecimal SHA-256 digest, and `text` MUST be a nonempty array of strings. Evidence MUST NOT store source text for outline inputs.
:::{req} evidence_coverage

For every `{impl}` and `{test}` reference in a project source file, including one in a requirement or example declaration, the evidence file for the referenced requirement or example MUST contain an input whose resolved source ranges cover the reference's file and line. A `{cite}` reference MUST NOT require coverage; it is discoverable through {cite}`requirements.authoring.reference_index`. Habeas MUST report every uncovered reference with its role, full name, source file, and line number.
